dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "Decision: Do not escalate or restate revenue on the supplied evidence."
"It is cheap and fully reversible: it writes no source record, makes no posting change, and its output can be discarded."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "This inference firmly resolves data-pipeline and fraud hypotheses" is too strong: reconciliation, unique identifiers, and accepted rows substantially weaken those hypotheses but do not by themselves prove absence of manipulation or every possible pipeline defect.
"with complete bank cash settlement" is not directly established by the cited import-log reconciliation to ledger unless the underlying file explicitly documents bank settlement.

"all 17 renewals ... correspond to genuine retail transaction dates" overstates what the email and dates prove; they support the posting-time explanation but do not independently establish transaction genuineness.

"Standardizing the reporting cadence prevents visual distortion across reporting periods" is a broad recommendation without a specific implementation or explicit instruction to use `effective_event_date` for downstream analytics.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The submission handled the main alternatives—duplicate revenue, manipulation, pipeline defect, and entitlement failure—by testing reconciliation and source-event uniqueness and by preserving entitlement and policy unknowns. It could have more explicitly treated legitimate event-time versus posting-time reporting as a continuing analytics risk even if no financial issue exists.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Complete and report the entitlement/duplicate-cash reconciliation explicitly, then state a firm downstream rule: use `effective_event_date` for event-time retention and trend analytics while retaining `posted_at` for posting and ledger reporting.

dimensions.name: Calibration and alternatives
citations: "While genuine deflection occurred for routine queries (29.1% balance checks, 21.3% pack info)"
"I cannot test whether failed-authentication customers contact SkyWave again without a read-only subscriber-level 7-day callback/recontact query."

dimensions.name: Usefulness and clarity
citations: "The single next action is one targeted, read-only 7-day repeat-contact/callback query reconciled to all NOVA sessions."
"Person: Farah Iqbal, Customer Care Operations, because she owns IVR journey stages, case-creation conditions, and the containment definition."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Apparent complaint reduction is heavily driven by 650 pre-authentication drops and automated ticket-creation suppression" is stronger than the evidence shown: the submission does not quantify how much of the ticket decline those sessions explain, and the email supports exclusion from the CareDesk view more directly than intentional suppression.

"Underlying network faults persisted at 8 to 10 major service events per month" overstates the cited service-event data unless those events are explicitly classified as network faults and major events.
"unresolved technical issues went unrecorded" treats authentication-stage abandonment as unresolved technical issues, although abandonment may also reflect benign exits or non-complaint journeys.

The submission does not establish that service-event exposure should move one-for-one with complaint cases; the divergence is useful diagnostic evidence but is not by itself proof of missed complaints.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The analyst handled the strongest benign alternative—that the pilot produced genuine self-service deflection for authenticated routine queries—by quantifying balance_check and pack_info stages. It did not fully handle the possibility that some authentication-stage abandonment was benign or unrelated to dissatisfaction, rather than a failed complaint journey.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Add end-to-end journey linkage and sampled call listening to the proposed repeat-contact query, so authentication-stage abandonment can be separated into resolved, recovered, repeat-contact, and genuinely unresolved or complaint-related outcomes rather than being inferred from case absence.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: “The 4 records occur on 27, 28, 29 May and 4 June; INV-17/03/22/09 each seen once, total duration 13 minutes.” Source: inverter_events.csv, rows 1–4, timestamp_local, inverter_id, duration_min.
“Constant columns: impact_mw=0 and cleared=yes: 0/4 rows open and 0/4 have nonzero generation loss.” Source: inverter_events.csv, rows 1–4, impact_mw, cleared.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The analyst connects short durations, self-cleared status, zero impact, and lack of recurrence across inverters to the decision not to escalate.

“Confirm completeness before treating it as representative; this is a data-scope check, not evidence of equipment fault.” This is a sound scope distinction, though the analysis relies primarily on one event-export channel rather than triangulating independent operational or communications data.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: “The export spans 27 May–4 June (9 calendar days) but contains only 4 rows and no plant-wide denominator or extraction filter.”
“Labels alone do not establish failure.”
The conclusion conditions closure on the result of an unfiltered pull and identifies recurrence, open faults, critical severity, or nonzero impact as decision-changing evidence.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: “Hold escalation and execute one cheap completeness check.”
“Run a read-only export query for 27 May–4 June without status filters.”
The proposed action is reversible, proportionate, and discriminates between an incomplete extract and a genuinely broader event population.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: “Do not escalate on this 4-row extract.”
“Labels justify checking export completeness, but do not justify an equipment investigation.”
This accurately reflects zero MW impact, rapid clearing, one-off inverter occurrences, and the rubric’s expectation not to invent a plant problem from a short communications warning.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: “Routine” is a reasonable characterization but remains an inference from a small extract; it should not be generalized until completeness is confirmed.
“Operational intervention ... is premature” is appropriately scoped to the available extract, but transient communications degradation is not ruled out by zero generation impact alone.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The four rows could be an incomplete or filtered export, or the 7-minute COMM_LINK_WARN could represent a transient communications-quality issue that did not affect generation. The analyst appropriately treats this as a completeness/low-priority quality check rather than evidence of equipment damage.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: After the unfiltered export, compare the warning’s interval with inverter communications or controller logs if it recurs, remains open, or shows associated telemetry gaps; this would distinguish a benign cleared alert from a real communications-quality issue.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: The submission cites `dispatch_blocks.csv`, identifies the relevant fields (`base_schedule_mw`, `submitted_schedule_mw`, `actual_mw`, `schedule_source`, and `dsm_rate_rs_kwh`), and provides reproducible calculations for both 31.6% and 17.6%.
It distinguishes the observations that 28 and 29 May are different dates from the inference that the difference is not causal proof.
It cites `DSM_Commercial_Extract.pdf` for the separate energy valuation and incomplete settlement information.

dimensions.name: Investigative reasoning
citations: The submission constructs the required same-day counterfactual: 'Applying the documented banded penalty to `base_schedule_mw` against the same actual generation gives about Rs 549,664, versus Rs 453,086 submitted.'
It cross-checks multiple deviation measures, including summed absolute block deviation and absolute net daily imbalance, and correctly notes that neither isolates the pilot.
It considers selection and timing, baseline variability, and commercial-settlement explanations rather than treating the headline anomaly as sufficient evidence.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: The submission labels the arithmetic confidence as 'High' but the causal interpretation as 'Medium' or unresolved, which is appropriately claim-specific.
It explicitly states that the 17.6% result is 'descriptive/model-based evidence for that day, not causal proof.'
It identifies decision-changing unknowns: pre-outcome selection and immutable timestamps, replication across matched pilot days, and reconciled net settlement data.

dimensions.name: Decision/action quality
citations: The recommendation to maintain current scope and hold national expansion is proportionate to the lack of causal and net-value evidence.
The proposed prospective, pre-registered matched high-wind shadow validation is discriminating and preserves operational constraints: 'zero control changes, zero commercial commitments.'
The next test includes both immutable pre-submission timestamps and net commercial settlement, directly addressing the principal uncertainties.

dimensions.name: Conclusion fit
citations: The judgment correctly distinguishes '31.6% valid arithmetic for two different days' from an unsupported causal claim.

It retains the smaller same-day modeled benefit rather than concluding that the pilot had no value: 'the submitted schedule containing 12 pilot revisions had a modeled penalty about 17.6% below the retained base schedule.'
The conclusion that evidence is insufficient for expansion accurately matches the supplied evidence and the stated limitations.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The phrase 'the stronger same-day modeled estimate' could be read as overstating evidentiary strength: it is a better-aligned counterfactual comparison than the cross-day headline, but it still relies on one day, 12 revised blocks, and the assumption that `base_schedule_mw` is a credible counterfactual.

The submission does not establish whether the 12 revisions were selected using information correlated with realized generation; it appropriately presents this as an unresolved limitation rather than a demonstrated fact.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 29 May reduction may reflect day-specific wind, forecast, timing, or block-selection conditions rather than the causal effect of the 12 pilot revisions. The same-day base-schedule comparison supports a potentially useful modeled benefit, but it cannot distinguish that interpretation without pre-registered replication and timing data.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Validate the 12 revision blocks with immutable pre-submission timestamps and a pre-registered matched-day or shadow comparison, while reconciling penalty, energy revenue, and pilot costs into a complete net-settlement measure.

dimensions.name: Decision safety
citations: "Place a reversible administrative hold on the preference claim."
"Treat the line as non-preferential (0.0% duty neutral) until documentary proof is verified, without initiating an irreversible voluntary disclosure."
"administrative holds precede any formal compliance escalation."

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "EU suppliers SUP-03/05/06 would allow linking active preference" is overstated: identifying an EU supplier alone does not establish preferential origin or satisfy the applicable originating-rule evidence.
"SUP-01 would confirm non-preferential MFN" is not fully supported by the cited materials because the shipment's actual supplier and the applicable duty treatment are not established.

"Valid declaration flips decision to clear as preferential" is too categorical; a supplier declaration may be necessary evidence but may not alone establish all product-specific preferential-origin requirements.
"Treat the line as non-preferential (0.0% duty neutral)" could conflate preferential status with duty rate and should be conditional on confirming the applicable tariff treatment.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The shipment may have been supplied by SUP-03, SUP-05, or SUP-06 and may therefore have supporting preferential-origin evidence in procurement folders or outside the register. The missing linkage establishes an evidence-control failure, not necessarily an invalid claim or fraud; alternatively, the shipment may have been supplied by a non-preferential source, in which case the claim would require correction after verification.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Make the action explicitly conditional on confirming the applicable tariff treatment and state that a supplier declaration must be checked against the product-specific originating rule rather than treated as automatically sufficient to clear preference.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: The statement that 70.6% of release times are definitively "snapshot artifact" or "defaulted" goes beyond the observed timestamp concentration and source-freshness timing unless an event-level audit has already established that semantics.

The claim that excluding the 02:10 rows produces an "evidence-to-release" median is potentially misnamed: the submission appears to use a lab-complete-to-release proxy, not the SOP's required-evidence-available timestamp.
The assertion that the 1.5-day headline represents a 45.5-hour receipt-to-release mean is numerically or semantically unclear and should reconcile the headline denominator and population.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: The 02:10 concentration may reflect a legitimate scheduled/interface commit time rather than wholly artificial release timing; some underlying workflow delay could still be real. The data supports withholding the KPI, but not attributing the full apparent delay to the interface without event-level timestamps.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Explicitly separate receipt-to-interface-commit, lab-complete-to-interface-commit, and true decision-time measures, then obtain a small event-level audit containing required-evidence availability and disposition/decision timestamps for the same batches across QCore and CertVault, with snapshot times reconciled.

dimensions.name: Evidence traceability
citations: "The 24 open requests total $166,495.60..." tied to `part_requests.csv`, all 24 rows, `qty`, `external_quote_usd`, and `status=OPEN`.
"The global stock snapshot is dated 26 June..." tied to `source_freshness.csv`, MaintStar-global and ProcureNet rows, and `spares_transfer_policy.md`.
Specific request IDs, part numbers, revisions, quantities, reservation states, and restriction files are cited throughout.

dimensions.name: Causal / investigative reasoning
citations: "The brief assumes search recall is the constraint, but semantic search is not the real problem."
"An exact join on manufacturer part numbers... retrieves every identified request. Remaining work is eligibility governed by... quantity, reservation... revision, UOM, qualification and freshness."

The submission tests alternatives involving revision mismatch, reservation, negative availability, and missing identifiers, but the broader conclusion about semantic search is based on only 24 requests and remains provisional.

dimensions.name: Calibration and uncertainty
citations: "Treat search results as candidates, not automatic transfers."
"‘Actionable now’ still requires current confirmation" because the global stock snapshot is older than the request export.
"Needs check" and "Not transferable on current evidence" distinguish evidence states, although the label "Actionable now" is somewhat stronger than the stale-snapshot evidence supports.

dimensions.name: Decision usefulness / reframing
citations: "Defend only the eight-request actionable slice, not gross value."
"Test search on the 11 blank-MPN requests."

The recommendation separates candidate value from actionable value, protects against revision/reservation/quantity errors, and proposes comparing exact matching with semantic search before committing to a system.

dimensions.name: Disconfirmation and rejected hypotheses
citations: "Every search hit represents a direct transfer opportunity": rejected" using reserved and zero-stock examples.
"Same part family means interchangeable": rejected" using revision-A versus revision-B evidence.
"available_qty_global=-1 means zero stock": rejected" using on-hand data and the maintenance-email sentinel explanation.
Each rejected hypothesis includes conditions under which it could be revived, such as a live CMMS check or documented approval.

dimensions.name: Questioning / next evidence
citations: The table requests targeted evidence for blank-MPN identity, live reservation/availability, revision and qualification approval, and semantic-search value.
For each unknown, it states how the evidence would change classification, rather than asking generically for more data.

unsupported_or_overstated_claims: "Semantic search is not the real problem" is broader than the evidence supports: exact MPN matching covers 13 requests, while semantic search may still add material value for the 11 blank-MPN or description-only requests.
Several rows are labeled "Actionable now" even though the submission acknowledges that the global MaintStar snapshot is stale and current availability still requires confirmation.
The claim that all 13 MPN requests have exact-join candidates is clearly attributed to the files but is not shown with row-level detail for each request.
per_question.strongest_alternative_interpretation: Semantic search may still be valuable as a candidate-generation layer for the 11 requests lacking MPNs and for description-only matches; exact matching demonstrates data-quality opportunity but does not establish that semantic search has little incremental recall or operational value.
per_question.single_most_valuable_next_improvement: Run a small, blinded comparison on the 11 blank-MPN requests using exact-MPN, normalized-description, and semantic retrieval, then have engineering verify identity, revision, UOM, qualification, and current availability; use the validated-match yield to decide whether to pilot semantic search.
